## GATE1 · GATE1-mint-lease — GATE1: minting handles into a lease carved under users

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: 4c450557056b8a6b750d0c2b7f062bed, ad9fe3d3e

Evidence: Settled by the Architect: Q1 -&gt; option (a), an endpoint maker run in users itself, whose users-stamped endpoints outlive it; (b) rejected (a system-class lease voids label non-interference). Q2/Q3/Q4 agreed. Rule committed on redoubt as ad9fe3d3e (docs/kernel/objects.md, mint); gate1 worktree reset onto it. GATE1 implementer to launch with these answers.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `c5fe3dd498e4e30fb045a423a94698dd` · 2026-09-30T02:12:39Z

> GATE1 (kernel containment gate) is resuming; the implementer raised a blocking design question before writing the hostile-lease program. The pages don't settle it, so it's yours.
> 
> Context: the gate carves hostile leases under a `sessions` budget under `users` (the launcher holds root/system/users). The steward, victim and program run in `system`. R9/`mint` only narrows: the budget named as a stamp must be the source's default stamp or below it (objects.md#mint), and `users` is beside `system` under `root`, so a `system`-stamped receive right cannot mint a handle into a lease under `users`.
> 
> The implementer's checkpoint (.worktrees/gate1/GATE1-checkpoint1.md, Q1) gives two options:
> (a, its recommendation) run an 'endpoint maker' once in `users`: it creates the victim's endpoints and the steward's progress endpoint (stamped and owned by `users`), which outlive the maker (an endpoint dies with its owner budget, not its process); the steward keeps receive-right copies and mints into the lease from those.
> (b) carve the sessions/lease budget under `system` — the implementer says this is against the page.
> 
> Decide from R9, budgets.md (the boot tree) and objects.md (endpoint ownership), or name a third way; flag any consequence for R21/blame or the real steward. Non-blocking, quick answers also welcome on Q2 (sub-agent churn children get no killed-notice under R10 step 3; judged by sessions' usage returning exactly), Q3 (driver's 256 samples span ~1s of a ~10s run; add a spacing parameter, default unchanged), Q4 (bystander share floor 100/120 of the window less R12's 50/1000).

### Architect · Answer

Event: `4c450557056b8a6b750d0c2b7f062bed` · 2026-09-30T02:18:19Z

> Q1 (blocking): option (a), with one precision. (b) rejected.
> 
> (b): a lease under `system` is `system`-class (class inherited, budgets.md), exempting the hostile agent from the kernel label check (R1) and voiding label non-interference (a tenet); it also contradicts the boot tree (sessions/leases under `users`).
> 
> (a) is right, from R9 + endpoint ownership: an endpoint dies with its owner budget, not its process (maker may exit); a receive-right copy keeps its stamp (R9), so the steward's `users`-stamped copy mints into a lease (lease ≤ users). Precision: the maker runs in `users` itself, never a child of it — a child's stamp is the leases' sibling, so mint into a lease is `NotPermitted`.
> 
> Third way already in the book: `init` (in `root`) makes its servers' endpoints stamped `root` and mints the manifest's badges (init.md#starting-the-servers); `root` is above everything, so a maker run in `root` (the program holds `root`) also works and is the full system's shape. (a) is the narrower stamp; either is accepted.
> 
> R21/blame: unchanged — the maker exits cleanly; keepers blame the call their thread serves; endpoints owned by `users` change only accounting/lifetime.
> 
> Real steward: same rule — its receive rights for minting into sessions/leases must be `root`-stamped (made by `init`), never its own `system` ones; the steward step mints from those copies.
> 
> Q2 — agreed: agent and sub-agent are created by the steward, their process objects charge to the steward's `system` budget and both get `killed` notices (R10 step 2); churn children have objects charged to a dying budget, freed with no notice (R10 step 3), judged by sessions' usage returning exactly.
> 
> Q3 — agreed: add the spacing parameter, default unchanged.
> 
> Q4 — agreed floor; if it misses, report numbers rather than lower it (it sits at the destruction-cost boundary, budget-destroy-cost.md).
> 
> Rule written on docs/kernel/objects.md (§mint).
